title: Localisation in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about languages and design: what people will read, what the web is written in, and how text changes when it's translated.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are.

outro.heading: Language is design.
paras: A product doesn't really arrive in a new market until people can use it in their own language, and every one of today's numbers shows how much design work that involves.

questions.q: CSA Research surveyed consumers in 29 countries. What share said they prefer to buy products with information in their own language?
questions.explain: 76% of the 8,709 shoppers surveyed prefer product information in their own language, even many who speak English well. Translation is part of the product, not an extra.
questions.source: CSA Research, Can't Read, Won't Buy – B2C, 2020

questions.q: About what share of all websites are in English?
questions.explain: About half of websites are in English, although only a small minority of the world's population speaks it as a first language. Arabic, with hundreds of millions of speakers, is used by only about 0.6% of websites.
questions.source: W3Techs, content language usage statistics, October 2026

questions.q: Scotland's 2022 census asked about Scottish Gaelic. How many people had some Gaelic skills, such as speaking, reading or understanding it?
questions.explain: 130,161 people had some Gaelic skills, up from about 87,000 in 2011. Bilingual road and station signs in Gaelic and English are a familiar sight in parts of Scotland.
questions.source: National Records of Scotland, Scotland's Census 2022

questions.q: CSA Research also asked how often people buy from websites in a language they don't read. What share said they never do?
questions.explain: 40% said they never buy from websites in other languages. For a company, an untranslated website can shut out a large part of the market.
questions.source: CSA Research, Can't Read, Won't Buy – B2C, 2020

questions.q: What share of all viewing on Netflix is of titles that aren't in English?
questions.explain: Non-English titles account for just over a third of all viewing on Netflix, with Korean, Spanish and Japanese titles among the most watched. Subtitles and dubbing helped turn local shows into global hits.
questions.source: Netflix, What We Watched: the second half of 2025, January 2026

questions.q: Unicode is the standard that lets computers show the world's writing systems. How many characters did version 17.0 (2025) contain?
questions.explain: Unicode 17.0 has 159,801 characters, from Latin and Arabic to Cherokee, plus emoji. Before Unicode, many scripts couldn't be shown on the same page.

questions.q: Arabic is one of the six official languages of the United Nations. When was it added?
questions.explain: On 18 December 1973 the UN General Assembly made Arabic one of its official and working languages; the date is now marked as UN Arabic Language Day. Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish had been official since 1946.
questions.source: United Nations, Ask DAG: What are the official languages of the United Nations? (GA resolution 3190 (XXVIII))

questions.q: Short texts grow most when English is translated. For a label of up to 10 characters, how much space does IBM's guidance say designers should allow?
questions.explain: Short labels can double or triple in length (200–300%); for long texts (over 70 characters) about 130% is usually enough. Buttons and menus designed tightly for English often break first.
questions.source: W3C Internationalization, Text size in translation (IBM guidelines)
